questions.enonce_markdown:
**Translate into French**

> Mbeki was resting under a tree with his wife, Ada. They were to go out in the afternoon with their children, who were waiting in the parlour. They will go and watch the first football game in the new stadium of their city.

> In the past, the rainy season started in March, but it was already April, and the heat was still unbearable. What is happening to our planet, Mbeki always wondered.

> One of his daughters had told him about climate change, something he hardly understood. He called out to her and when she came, asked her:

> "Patou, I don't understand this climate thing! What do you say teachers tell you in class?"

> "Daddy," Patou answered. "Our geography teacher says the seasons are irregular because people fell trees but don't replace them. When human beings will learn to plant trees, the seasons will be more regular."
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model translation**

Mbeki se reposait sous un arbre avec sa femme, Ada. Ils devaient sortir dans l'après-midi avec leurs enfants, qui attendaient dans le salon. Ils iraient voir le premier match de football dans le nouveau stade de leur ville.

Autrefois, la saison des pluies commençait en mars, mais on était déjà en avril et la chaleur était toujours insupportable. « Que se passe-t-il sur notre planète ? », se demandait sans cesse Mbeki.

Une de ses filles lui avait parlé du changement climatique, une chose qu'il comprenait à peine. Il l'appela et, quand elle vint, lui demanda :

« Patou, je ne comprends pas cette histoire de climat ! Que dis-tu de ce que les professeurs vous racontent en classe ? »

« Papa, répondit Patou. Notre professeur de géographie dit que les saisons sont irrégulières parce que les gens abattent des arbres mais ne les remplacent pas. Quand les êtres humains apprendront à planter des arbres, les saisons seront plus régulières. »

**Translation points**

| Point | Trap | Correct form |
|---|---|---|
| Past narration, description of the scene | Using the passé composé for states and ongoing actions | Imparfait: *se reposait*, *attendaient*, *commençait*, *était* |
| "They were to go out" | *Ils étaient pour sortir* | *Ils devaient sortir* (*devoir* in the imparfait expresses a planned event) |
| "They will go and watch" (the source slips into the future inside a past narrative) | Switching suddenly to the present | Future in the past (conditional): *Ils iraient voir*; *Ils allaient aller voir* is also accepted, and a plain future (*Ils iront voir*) can be accepted as a faithful rendering of the source |
| "In the past" | *Dans le passé* word for word | *Autrefois* (or *Dans le temps*, *Jadis*) |
| "it was already April" | *c'était déjà avril* | *on était déjà en avril* (*en* with months, no article) |
| "the heat was still unbearable" | Putting "still" in the wrong place | *la chaleur était toujours insupportable* (*toujours* or *encore*, after the verb) |
| "What is happening to our planet, Mbeki always wondered" | *Quoi se passe...* | *Que se passe-t-il sur notre planète ?*, *se demandait Mbeki* (inversion after the quotation) |
| "had told him about climate change" | *avait dit lui de* | Plus-que-parfait with the indirect object pronoun: *lui avait parlé du changement climatique* (*parler de*, not *dire de*) |
| "something he hardly understood" | *quelque chose il comprenait à peine* | *une chose qu'il comprenait à peine* (relative pronoun *que*; *à peine* for "hardly") |
| "He called out to her and when she came, asked her" | Mixing tenses without a reason | A series of completed actions: passé simple (*appela*, *vint*, *demanda*) or passé composé throughout |
| "I don't understand this climate thing!" | *cette chose de climat* | *cette histoire de climat* (familiar, as in the source) |
| "What do you say teachers tell you in class?" | Word for word: *Quoi tu dis que professeurs disent...* | *Que dis-tu de ce que les professeurs vous racontent en classe ?*; *Qu'est-ce que les professeurs vous disent en classe ?* is also accepted |
| "Daddy" | *Daddy* kept in English | *Papa* |
| "people fell trees but don't replace them" | *tombent*, or forgetting the pronoun *les* | *abattent* (or *coupent*) *des arbres mais ne les remplacent pas* (negation with the object pronoun before the verb) |
| "When human beings will learn to plant trees, the seasons will be more regular" | Using the present after *quand* by analogy with English rules | French also uses the future after *quand*: *Quand les êtres humains apprendront à planter des arbres, les saisons seront plus régulières* |

**Marking note**

The text is short, so every sentence counts. Credit goes to accuracy (tenses, agreements, accents) and to natural French rather than word-for-word translation. Keep the quotation marks and the punctuation of the direct speech. The source contains small slips of its own ("will go and watch" in a past narrative, "What do you say teachers tell you", "When human beings will learn"); any reasonable, correct French rendering of these is accepted.

**Common mistakes**

1. Leaving out a sentence or part of a sentence (for example "something he hardly understood"). Everything in the source must be translated.
2. Using one tense for the whole text. The scene is described in the imparfait and plus-que-parfait, while the events are in the passé simple or passé composé.
